message.content:
### Tenant Rights in Texas (as of 2024) | Area | Key Rights | How to Exercise Them | |------|------------|----------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• Deposit must be returned within **30 days** after the lease ends, unless the landlord provides a written itemized list of deductions. | • Keep a copy of the lease and any move‑in inspection report.
• Request a written itemized statement if you believe deductions are incorrect. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain the property in a safe, sanitary, and livable condition (e.g., plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity). | • Report problems in writing (email or letter) and keep copies.
• If the landlord fails to fix issues, you may withhold rent, repair and deduct, or file a complaint with the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA). | | **Rent Increases** | • No statutory limit on rent increases, but the landlord must give **30 days’ written notice** for a month‑to‑month lease or **90 days’ notice** for a fixed‑term lease. | • Review the lease for any rent‑increase clauses.
• Verify that the notice period is respected. | | **Lease Termination** | • Landlord must provide **30 days’ written notice** to terminate a month‑to‑month lease.
• For a fixed‑term lease, the landlord can only terminate for cause (e.g., non‑payment, violation of lease). | • Keep a copy of the lease and any termination notices.
• If you receive a notice, you can negotiate or seek legal advice. | | **Right to Privacy** | • Landlord must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hours) before entering the unit, except in emergencies. | • Document any unannounced entries; you can file a complaint if the landlord violates this right. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income (e.g., public assistance). | • File a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights (TCHR) if you suspect discrimination. | | **Repair and Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to repair a major issue, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from your rent, provided you follow the proper procedure. | • Keep receipts and provide the landlord with a written notice of the repair and deduction. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must follow the Texas Property Code for eviction, including proper notice and filing a lawsuit if necessary. | • If you receive an eviction notice, you have the right to respond in court. | | **Fair Housing** | • Landlords must comply with federal Fair Housing Act and Texas Fair Housing Act. | • File a complaint with TCHR or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) if you believe your rights were violated. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord must provide a written statement of who is responsible for utilities. | • Keep copies of utility bills and lease clauses. | | **Lease Renewal** | • Landlord must provide a written renewal offer if they intend to renew the lease. | • Negotiate terms and keep a copy of the renewal agreement. | --- #### Practical Steps to Protect Your Rights 1. **Document Everything** - Keep copies of the lease, move‑in inspection reports, correspondence, and receipts for repairs. 2. **Know the Law** - Familiarize yourself with the Texas Property Code (Title 8, Chapter 91) and the Texas Fair Housing Act. 3. **Communicate in Writing** - Whenever possible, communicate with your landlord in writing (email or certified mail) so you have a record. 4. **Seek Legal Advice** - If you face a dispute, consult a tenant‑rights attorney or a local legal aid organization. 5. **File Complaints** - If you believe your rights are being violated, file a complaint with the TDHCA, TCHR, or HUD. --- #### Useful Resources | Resource | What It Offers | |----------|----------------| | **Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA)** | Information on tenant rights, landlord responsibilities, and how to file complaints. | | **Texas Commission on Human Rights (TCHR)** | Handles discrimination complaints. | | **U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)** | Federal fair housing resources. | | **Legal Aid of North Texas** | Free legal assistance for low‑income tenants. | | **Texas Tenant Rights Hotline** | Phone support for tenant questions. | --- **Disclaimer:** This information is general in nature and not legal advice. For specific legal questions, consult a qualified attorney.
